name: Tank Yard v1.1.0
body:
# Tank Yard v1.1.0

The Arena Workshop gains effects: decor that floats, sways, pulses, changes color and grows, launch pads, sounds and screen shake. Bacteria's pocket dimension becomes a maze of rooms with doubles that hunt you down. Scripts and JSON packs can use every new piece. Everything in [v1.0.1](v1.0.1.md) is included.

## Workshop effects

- **Animate decor** plays a looping animation on a group's decor: **Bob**, **Sway**, **Throb**, **Shake** or **Orbit**, each with its own size and pace. The five play together, so one group can bob and sway at once, and changing the pace never makes it jump.
- **Tint decor** mixes a color into a group's decor, lights and particles. A short tint that goes back makes a flash.
- **Scale decor** draws a group's decor and emitters from 0 to 400% of their placed size, particles included.
- **Stop group** halts a group's moves, turns, fades, tints, sizes and animations where they are and cancels its trip back.
- **Shake screen** shakes the views of the tanks inside a trigger's area. Players' **Camera shake** setting scales it, and Reduced motion turns it off.
- **Play sound** plays one of eight sounds at a trigger: Chime, Bell, Alarm, Switch, Whoosh, Rumble, Fanfare and Thump. Players hear it by distance, at their Effects volume.
- Tint, Scale and Animate play like motions, with a length, an easing curve and **Go back after**. **On arrive** watches them too.
- **Launch pads** fling tanks along their direction, then let them coast for a moment before steering takes over. Prediction uses the server's own code, so launches feel immediate online.
- A new **Effects** tab in the palette holds thirteen ready-made pieces: Float, Sway, Throb, Orbit, Quiver, Flash, Alarm, Dye, Grow, Stop, Quake, Chime and Siren.
- The logic preview plays effects: the canvas shakes when the test tank is caught in a Shake screen, and Play sound triggers play through your speakers.
- Effects change only how decor looks. Blocks, pads and trigger areas keep their shape and place, and Reduced motion holds animations still while keeping colors and sizes.

## Bacteria

- The pocket dimension is now a grid of rooms with aligned walls. Doorways use several positions along the room grid, and the walls continue past the edge of the maze.
- Soft, translucent ceiling lights hang above your tank with a gentle parallax. A few fixtures flicker and some have died.
- Up to three doubles of your tank wake after a short pause and follow you through the rooms. If one catches you, you're forced out early. They don't shoot, and only the server moves them.
- Bacteria's model has new shoulder plates that leave your team color visible.

## Modding

- New script functions: `tint_map_group`, `scale_map_group`, `animate_map_group`, `stop_map_group`, `shake_view` and `play_sound`, and `map_pose` to read where a group's motions have put it.
- JSON hooks gain `map_tint`, `map_animate`, `map_stop`, `shake_view` and `play_sound`, and `map_motion` accepts `scale`.
- JSON maps gain the `launch` pad and the `tint`, `scale`, `animate`, `stop`, `shake` and `sound` trigger actions. New fields are left out of exported maps when unused.
- Workshop plugins see the new trigger fields, and `editor.free_group` skips groups that effects use.
- A new example pack, [`mods/arena_fx`](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/tree/v1.1.0/mods/arena_fx), rings a bell at the start of each round, marks wrecks and kill streaks, and gives maps an alarm they can sound by name.

## Tutorials

- The [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/map-editor.md#effects) covers every effect and palette piece.
- The [motions tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/motions-tutorial.md) adds a step that gives the gatehouse a launch pad, a floating lantern, a door chime and a tremor as the barricades land.
- A new [Animate and effects walkthrough](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/effects-tutorial.md) has matching playable site examples and a bundled [Effects Lab map](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/tree/v1.1.0/mods/effects_lab) you can play or import into the workshop.

## Sandbox and hosting

- Sandbox has a centered toolbox with tank previews, search by name or ID, tier filters, touchpad paging and separate player and spawn controls. Escape closes it, and search input takes priority over gameplay shortcuts.
- Dedicated hosts can create a token-authenticated config with `--secure --write-config`, check it with `--check-config`, and issue short-lived UDP invitations with `--issue-token`. Keys are never printed, and existing credential files are never replaced.
- Invalid private config errors no longer quote credential lines.
- The multiplayer load tool supports runs up to 24 hours, scheduled reconnects and JSON reports, with bounded timing storage.
- Local crash reports survive the next launch. `tankyard --diagnostics-path` prints their folder; reports are never uploaded automatically.
- Menu pages and bot decision subsystems are split into smaller modules. Additional sandbox checks cover hostile effect arguments, module cycles, path escapes and isolation between packs.

## Compatibility

Protocol **28** carries the doubles and the new effects. Update clients, servers and any separate relays together; 1.0.1 and earlier cannot join a 1.1.0 server, and older peers receive an update notice. Maps from earlier versions open unchanged. Maps that use launch pads or effects need 1.1.0 to open and play.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.0.1
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.0.1

Bacteria slips into a private pocket dimension, the motions tutorial has a video, and doors and returning motions behave more reliably. Everything in [v1.0.0](v1.0.0.md) is included.

## Bacteria

- A new level-55 tank, reached from Specter or Wisp, with twin alternating cannons and a **ten-second pocket dimension**.
- The entry sound and brief blackout lead into a private, Backrooms-inspired maze with yellow wallpaper, worn carpet, fluorescent lights and eerie room tones. Ceiling fixtures pass above the tank, with light pools on the carpet and slight parallax. The textures and recorded light hum are CC0 assets.
- Repair 40% of your maximum hull health over the visit and reposition through the maze. You cannot fight, take damage or capture objectives inside. Carried cores drop and deployed weapons clear on entry.
- The cooldown is 40 seconds from entry, leaving thirty seconds outside between visits. A countdown and a small return ring announce your return.
- Sounds are local, follow volume settings and fade on return. Reduced motion keeps lights steady. [Bacteria guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/bacteria.md).

## Workshop

- Doors and faders with **Go back after** return home even if another tank arrives while they are open or on their way back. A new arrival extends the wait without moving the resting point.
- The palette's **Door** moves its group to a fixed offset, so repeated arrivals keep it open at the same place.
- **On arrive** no longer acts when a motion has nowhere to go, such as a door told to open while it is already open. An interrupted motion still does not count as arriving.
- Particles' **Fade out** now controls their fade.
- Motion destinations and portal exits have diamond handles, matching the editor's guides.

## Tutorials

- The [motions tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/motions-tutorial.md) builds a gatehouse with a sliding door, moving cover, chained motions, lights and particles.
- Its [video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/motions-tutorial.mp4) runs for 2 minutes 15 seconds, with English captions and seven chapters on the [website](https://robertflexx.github.io/tankyard-site/#motions-video). Choose **Motions** above the workshop's player.
- The website's [interactive motions guide](https://robertflexx.github.io/tankyard-site/#motions) demonstrates every curve and mode, all ten Motion pieces, chained motions, lights and particle presets.

## Compatibility

Protocol **27** adds the pocket timer and ability. Update clients, servers and any separate relays together; 1.0.0 and earlier cannot join a 1.0.1 server. Older peers receive an update notice. Existing 1.0 maps open unchanged.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.0.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.0.0

Tank Yard 1.0 is here: sliding doors, lifts and moving cover glide in the workshop, lights glow like real lamps, particles gain new shapes, and tanks and bosses look sharper.

Thank you to everyone who played, hosted, built maps and reported bugs on the way here.

## Motions

- Four new trigger actions animate a group. **Move group** glides it by a distance, and **Move group to** glides it to a place measured from where the map puts it. **Turn decor** and **Fade decor** turn or fade its decor. A group's blocks, pads, decor and trigger areas move together, and moving cover pushes tanks, shapes and bosses out of its way.
- Each motion has a length, one of eleven easing curves (Linear, Sine, Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint, Expo, Circ, Back, Elastic and Bounce) and a mode (ease in, ease out, in and out, out and in). The Object tab draws the curve and plays it. **Go back after** plays the motion in reverse later, for doors that shut and lifts that come back down.
- **On arrive** acts when a group's motion ends, so motions can follow one another: a lift rises, then its door opens.
- Select a Move trigger to see where it sends its group, and drag the diamond to set the distance. The logic preview plays motions and outlines where each moved group belongs.
- The new **Motion** tab in the palette holds ready-made Door, Shuttle, Piston, Lift, Home, Drop, Spinner, Fader, Blink and Then pieces.
- Scripts can call `move_map_group`, `turn_map_group` and `fade_map_group`, and JSON hooks have a `map_motion` action.
- Moving cover adds almost no network traffic: snapshots carry each motion rather than every wall's position, and every client plays the same glide. Bots re-plan their routes while cover moves.

The [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#motions) explains motions, and the [modding guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.0/docs/modding.md#motions) has the map format.

## Lights and particles

- Lights brighten what lies under them: strongly in dark arenas and softly in light ones. **Flicker** makes a light waver like a flame or a failing lamp. The Decor tab has new Torch, Neon and Lantern presets.
- Particles can be soft or star-shaped, glow, drift sideways and twinkle. They can start anywhere in the emitter, inside its ellipse, along its outline or at its center. There are six new presets: Fireflies, Smoke, Snow, Glitter, Fountain and Pulse.
- Maps crowded with lights draw the extra ones more simply rather than slowing the frame, as maps crowded with particles already did.

## Workshop

- The workshop remembers your palette tab and item, the inspector tab, the Hidden and Animate switches, the logic preview's speed and where you were looking in the map, along with panel sizes.
- **Ctrl+Shift+A** selects everything like the selection, such as every torch or every speed pad.

## Tanks and bosses

- Automatic turrets sharing one mount are drawn as a single turret with a ringed cap, so their barrels no longer cross over each other. Fortress Array, Palisade, Tri-Sniper, Interceptor and Monolith look much cleaner.
- Boss armor has a raised rim. Wounded bosses glow amber, then pulse red in their last phase. Defender's turrets no longer cross over one another.

## Other changes

- On FreeBSD, the graphics settings explain that NVIDIA ships DLSS only for Linux and Windows.
- `tankyard-models --bosses --phase 3` draws bosses in a later phase.
- In workshop plugins, `editor.free_group` skips groups that motions and On arrive triggers use.
- Creator and central-owner identities are verified without asking only on the official server, servers on the same computer and games you host. Any other server asks first, so a server cannot pass your proof on to another server without your consent.

## Compatibility

Protocol **26**. Servers and players on 1.0 play only with each other, so players on 0.15 or 0.16 need to update before joining. Hosts should update their servers and relays together. Maps from earlier versions open unchanged, but maps saved or exported from 1.0 need 1.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.16.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.16.0

Workshop gates take several conditions, watchers and sequences arrive, navigation suits trackpads, busy servers run lighter, and Tank Yard now runs natively on FreeBSD.

## Map logic

- A trigger can check up to four conditions: a counter, whether a group is shown, how many tanks are inside its area, or the round time. Combine them as All (AND), Any (OR), Not all (NAND), None (NOR) or Just one (XOR).
- A shut gate can send an otherwise signal, which makes it an if/else. New otherwise signals pick a free channel.
- Watchers fire when a counter changes, a group is shown or hidden, or a boss is defeated. Sequence signals the next of a run of channels each time, and Reset triggers lets a group's triggers start afresh.
- Press P for the live Logic tab. It can step, change speed, edit counters, switch groups, send signals and test a boss defeat. Each condition card shows whether it holds and whether the gate is open.
- Logic and Gates are separate palette tabs. Gates holds ready-made AND, OR, XOR and if/else pieces, levers, sequences, watchers and resets. Wires show what each trigger depends on, and labels make room for each other when crowded.
- Scripts can call `reset_map_triggers(group)`, and the bundled Logic Kit adds a Lever bank tool.
- The [logic gates tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/logic-gates-tutorial.md) builds a two-lever vault step by step, and the [video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/logic-gates-tutorial.mp4) shows it in under two minutes.

## Workshop navigation

- Pan (4) moves the view with a plain drag. In Pan, arrows and WASD move the view even with objects selected.
- The Scroll setting chooses Auto, Trackpad or Mouse. With a trackpad, two fingers pan, and Ctrl or Cmd with scrolling zooms around the pointer. Pan and zoom speeds go from 0.25× to 3×, and 100% resets the zoom. The workshop remembers these settings.
- Zoom follows how far you scroll instead of jumping a full step for any movement.
- Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through overlapping objects under the pointer. Resize handles and panel dividers are easier to grab.

## Scrolling everywhere

- Menus, chat, the lobby and mod lists, the mod viewer and the tank tree scroll smoothly with trackpads and step evenly with wheels, on macOS, Windows, Wayland and X11. Ordinary wheels no longer scroll slowly on Wayland.

## Servers

- Projectile, wall and navigation checks skip distant objects. In a local test with 64 players and 24 bots on a maze map, 99th-percentile tick time fell from about 3.3 to 1.8 ms.
- Starting a server lists the addresses players join from this computer, the local network and the internet. Every option has clearer help.
- Linux, macOS and FreeBSD archives include `host-server.sh`, which writes a settings file on first run and then starts the server with it. The systemd unit keeps settings, bans and logs in `/var/lib/tankyard`. The [hosting guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/hosting.md) walks through installing, configuring, opening the port and running a service.

## FreeBSD

- FreeBSD 15 and newer on amd64 get their own build of the game, server, relay and tools, made on FreeBSD itself. Install the sound plugins with `pkg install alsa-plugins`, then run `fetch -o - https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`.
- The game uses X11 and OpenGL with Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. With NVIDIA, it queues one frame ahead, as on Linux. DLSS is available only on Linux and Windows.
- The FreeBSD archive carries an rc.d script that runs the server as its own user, restarts it if it stops, reopens its log when rotated, and can run several named servers.
- The [FreeBSD guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.16.0/docs/freebsd.md) covers NVIDIA setup, sound, hosting and building from source.

## Fixes

- Leaving a WebSocket server through the relay reaches the server at once on FreeBSD, instead of after a timeout.
- The installer works without curl on FreeBSD, using `fetch` and `sha256`.

Protocol **25**, as in 0.15. Players on any 0.15 or 0.16 build play together. Maps that use the new logic need a 0.16 server, or 0.16 to play them offline; older servers refuse them with a clear message. Maps without it save exactly as before.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.15.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.15.2

Menus follow your frame limit, frame limits hold their exact rate, and the Arena Workshop tutorial and a full plugin guide now live in the docs.

## Frame rate

- The title screen and menus run at the selected frame limit instead of stopping near 60 fps. With VSync on and no limit, they follow the display's refresh rate. Battery saver still holds games to 60 fps and menus to 30.
- Frame limits now count the time spent presenting each frame and keep a steady schedule, so 60 and 144 fps limits run at 60 and 144 rather than overshooting or falling short. The opening animation uses the same pacing.

## Arena Workshop

- When a plugin tool removes objects and doesn't choose what to select, the selection keeps only objects that still exist.
- The [tutorial video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/arena-workshop-tutorial.mp4) is in the repository's docs, linked from the README and the [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/map-editor.md). Game packages leave it out to keep downloads small.
- The new [editor plugin guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v0.15.2/docs/editor-plugins.md) covers installing plugins, a complete first tool, pack layout, every parameter type, the `ctx` API, coordinates, group and counter allocation, map checks, execution limits, distribution and troubleshooting. A test runs its example exactly as printed.

## Documentation

- Guides, server measurements and earlier release notes are tidied for players, mod authors, hosts and maintainers. The bundled Workshop Toolkit and Logic Kit READMEs link to the plugin guide.

Protocol **25**, as in v0.15.0 and v0.15.1. Clients and servers from those versions play together.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v0.15.1
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v0.15.1

Arena Workshop gains Luau plugins, resizable panels, more map logic and an updated tutorial. Voice and snapshot delivery get several fixes.

## Arena Workshop

- Drag the inspector and dock edges to resize them, double-click to reset, or press **\\** to hide the panels. The workshop remembers its layout and view preferences.
- Resize a whole selection with its handles. Hold Shift to keep proportions or Alt to resize around the center. Thin selections keep enough space to drag them. Frame the selection with Shift+F, mirror a copy with M, repeat a move with Ctrl+D, and lock groups while editing around them.
- Enabled, reviewed packs can add Luau tools and map checks in the **Tools** tab. Each tool edits a copy of the map, validates its result and applies it as one undo step. Ctrl+R repeats the last tool. Workshop Toolkit provides repeat, ring, frame, snap and mirror tools. Logic Kit builds switch doors, countdowns and sequences.
- The Check tab includes plugin advice and object budgets. The toolkit's gap check handles touching walls and dense maps.

[Workshop guide](../map-editor.md) · [Plugin API](../modding.md#workshop-plugins) · [Updated tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/releases/download/v0.15.1/arena-workshop-tutorial.mp4)

## Map logic and scripting

- Add While inside, On empty and On destroy triggers. Actions can set counters, choose a random signal, repair or damage tanks, and award points.
- Gate triggers on counter comparisons or group visibility. Calculate supports arithmetic, counter operands, random values and a 0/1 flip. Use **Fire** to test an action directly in the editor preview.
- Script actions raise the Luau `map_event` event. Scripts can read map counters and group visibility, send map signals, change counters, and show or hide groups. Script requests apply on the next simulation tick.
- Malformed counter and random-signal settings are rejected safely, including extreme integer values.

## Voice, networking and bosses

- Voice uses a 48 kbps Opus target, a microphone high-pass filter, a speech lead-in and hangover, adaptive playback buffering, fades and a soft limiter for mixed voices. The server reuses listener calculations across each received batch.
- Late snapshots preserve the newest cached wall geometry. Changed walls repeat in four snapshots, with periodic recovery resends, reducing traffic from maps with moving gates.
- Bastion gains a fortress hull, corner towers and a rotating central gun. Sentinel, Skirmisher and Trapper receive restrained armor details.

Protocol **25**, as in v0.15.0. The server sends clients map geometry with server-side triggers removed, so v0.15.0 players can join a v0.15.1 server using the new logic. Maps and editor plugins using the new APIs require v0.15.1 on the machine running them.
